title: Spaceship Material Calibration Lab
description: You are inside a spaceship hallway that serves as a material calibration laboratory. Five ShaderBalls are mounted on pedestals along the corridor, each representing a hull panel zone. You must mix and apply custom PBR shader parameters across all five balls while maintaining a total energy conservation budget, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that loads both GLB assets. Place the space_ship_hallway as the environment. Inside the hallway, position 5 instances of ShaderBall evenly spaced along the corridor on small emissive pedestals. Camera starts at one end of the hallway looking down the corridor; use OrbitControls constrained to stay inside the hallway bounds. Add dim blue-white point lights along the ceiling for sci-fi ambiance and one directional light simulating emergency lighting. Each ShaderBall gets a custom ShaderMaterial with uniforms for: metalness (0-1), roughness (0-1), emissive intensity (0-1), fresnel strength (0-2), and tint color (RGB). Implement a fragment shader that combines a PBR-like BRDF with fresnel rim lighting and emissive glow using these uniforms. Display a bottom HUD panel showing the selected ball index and sliders for all 5 parameters. Clicking a ShaderBall selects it with an outline glow post-effect or wireframe overlay. Enforce an energy conservation law: the sum of metalness + emissive intensity across all 5 balls must not exceed 3.0. If a slider adjustment would violate this, clamp the value and flash a red warning on the HUD. Implement a coupling rule: adjusting roughness on one ball automatically nudges the roughness of its two neighbors by 25 percent of the delta in the opposite direction, simulating thermal equilibrium. Add a color picker for tint that writes to the uniform vec3. Implement an undo/redo stack (at least 20 levels) triggered by keyboard shortcuts Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, storing full state snapshots of all 5 balls' parameters. Each parameter change counts as one interaction step. Show a small undo/redo counter on the HUD. Add a 'Randomize All' button that sets all balls to random valid parameters respecting the energy budget, counting as one undoable action. The total intended workflow is 10-14 steps: select balls, tweak parameters, observe coupling, undo mistakes, randomize, and refine.
